about: Audit targets for nulltest_audit.py. Every target names the exact download URL, the exact field mapping, and what kind of label it carries. A target with no url, or one that fails to fetch, is reported as such — you cannot audit what nobody published, and that is a finding too. OUR OWN BATTERIES ARE THE FIRST TWO ROWS AND BOTH FAIL.
disqualified_means: On this corpus a model-free classifier recovers the labels from surface form above what label-shuffling produces, so a model-based score on it needs a surface control to be interpretable. It is NOT a finding of error or misconduct by the authors, NOT a claim that the paper's conclusion is wrong, and NOT a statement about the method the paper proposes. Several of these corpora predate the practice of publishing a surface control. Ours do too, and ours fail.

label_kinds.real_vs_fabricated_entity: the item is an entity string. A surface hit means invented entities are spelled differently from real ones. This is the case the instrument was built for.
label_kinds.true_vs_false_statement: the item is a whole sentence. A surface hit may reflect TEMPLATING — how the false statements were generated — rather than anything about the entities. Still a real confound for a probe trained on those sentences, but a different claim, and this table says which kind each row is.
label_kinds.known_vs_unknown_real_entity: both classes are REAL entities from one registry, split by date. A surface hit means the registry's language drifted between the two periods, not that the fabricated half was generated differently — there is no fabricated half. A row of this kind is only meaningful if the model actually knows the known half; see prominence-people-v1, whose label validity was measured on the live model rather than assumed.

targets.name: aperture/verifydomain-claims-147
targets.paper: Aperture / Project Forty Two — the battery behind our own front-page headline, withdrawn
targets.note: ours, and it was our headline. 147 claims, 36 coined fakes. DISQUALIFIED: all three scorable cells separate, lexicality A* 0.967. It led the home page for months while living on one machine outside version control, never served and never floored. Recovered, floored, published and withdrawn on 2026-07-25. Being a true_vs_false_statement corpus, the surface hit may reflect how the false claims were GENERATED rather than anything about the entities.

targets.name: aperture/prominence-people-v2
targets.paper: Aperture / Project Forty Two — the first battery of ours that clears its own surface floor
targets.note: ours. Both classes real people; label 0 = high en.wikipedia pageviews, label 1 = low, drawn from that same person's own categories and matched on surname initial (78/78) and name length. PASSES: worst A* 0.554, family-adjusted p 0.8186. Power demonstrated (+1 char per item -> DISQUALIFIED at A* 0.750, p 0.0017). Label validity measured on the live model, not assumed: familiarity AUROC 0.999671 famous-over-obscure - NOT 1.000, and not threshold-separable (2 of 6084 pairs invert).

targets.name: aperture/prominence-people-v1
targets.paper: Aperture / Project Forty Two — a battery that PASSED this floor and was still broken
targets.note: ours, retained as evidence. PASSES at worst A* 0.602, adjusted p 0.2246 - and is defective anyway: a fifth probe outside the shipped four, the surname's initial letter, recovers the labels at A* 0.661, because the builder measured the alphabetically-first 200 members of each Wikipedia category and biography categories sort by surname. Superseded by v2. In this table because a floor that cannot be shown to miss things will be mistaken for a proof of correctness.

targets.name: aperture/postcutoff-trials-v1
targets.paper: Aperture / Project Forty Two — surface-blind by construction: BOTH classes real, split by registry date
targets.note: ClinicalTrials.gov v2 brief titles. label 0 = first posted 2023-01..2024-06 (the model may have seen it), label 1 = 2026-04..2026-06 (it cannot have). Both halves are REAL titles from one registry, so surface statistics match by construction and neither half is a near-copy of the other. Length-matched; titles containing an explicit year removed.
